page: Microsoft Azure E64-16ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained-core architecture designed for memory-intensive workloads that require lower core counts for software licensing optimization. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a substantial 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, along with 2577 GB of bundled local SSD storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2916.18, placing it in the top 25 percent. Multi-core performance is balanced at 21997.48 on stress-ng and 9969.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Cached memory read throughput reaches 1045.32 GB/sec, while uncached large-block throughput drops to 38.96 GB/sec read and 22.66 GB/sec write. In-memory operations show reliable throughput, yielding 15.88 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database score of 6967.74.

The primary efficiency tradeoff of the E64-16ads_v5 lies in its high memory-to-vCPU allocation. By reducing active vCPUs to 16 while retaining the full 512 GB memory pool and local NVMe-equivalent SSD capacity of a 64-core chassis, organizations can lower per-core licensing expenses. This makes the instance suitable for large relational database engines such as Microsoft SQL Server and Oracle, extensive in-memory caching tiers, and enterprise resource planning systems that demand large memory capacity without requiring excessive core concurrency.

However, uncached memory bandwidth remains modest at 38.96 GB/sec. This configuration offers an advantageous balance for enterprise relational databases, large-scale caching clusters, and analytics engines requiring high memory capacity over raw parallel processor counts.
